input.quote: This Agreement will automatically be renewed for periods of twelve (12) months unless either Party gives six (6) months written notice of its intent to terminate this Agreement. Such renewals shall continue for successive periods under the same terms and conditions, unless otherwise agreed in writing by both Parties.
input.rationale: Both renewal clauses auto-renew but impose non-renewal notice windows far beyond the 60-day fallback: Base Agreement §4.0 requires six months (~180 days) against 12-month renewal terms, and Attachment §2.0 requires twelve months (~365 days) against six-month renewal terms, so the Attachment can effectively never be exited at term end. Notice windows longer than 90 days are walk-away territory, so this fails the fallback on a material term. Renewal pricing is not a problem: both clauses provide that renewals continue \"under the same terms and conditions\", so no unilateral price increase is permitted and no cap is needed. We therefore make the minimal fallback fix — shortening each notice window to sixty (60) days — rather than upgrading to preferred (30-day opt-out, vendor reminder, CPI cap).

proposal.comment: [Playbook] The six-month (Base Agreement) and twelve-month (Attachment) non-renewal notice windows are far longer than our 60-day fallback, and the Attachment's twelve-month notice exceeds its own six-month renewal term. We have shortened both windows to sixty days; renewals otherwise continue on the same terms and conditions, so pricing remains unchanged.
proposal.summary: Shorten non-renewal notice to 60 days in Base Agreement §4.0 and Attachment §2.0

mappings.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer's non-renewal notice window is no more than 60 days.
If renewal permits price increases, each increase is capped at 5 percent.
mappings.quote: Such renewals shall continue for successive periods under the same terms and conditions, unless otherwise agreed in writing by both Parties.
